A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReviseEval work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison; v2 retains appendices A-I and adds J-P.

before.justification: v1 reports original ReviseEval experiments on NLG and instruction-following benchmarks, including correlations, accuracies, bias analyses, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds reference-correctness assessments, multiple-reference experiments, and additional benchmark evaluations.

M1.justification: The core procedure, equations (1)-(4), and original prompts remain unchanged. Appendix L adds Fine-Grained ReviseEval: separate aspect-specific revisions produce multiple references, followed by separate evaluations aggregated through majority voting or mean scores. This is a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: The original training and evaluation coverage is retained. Appendices K, N, and O add JudgeBench, RewardBench, and adapted GPQA and Omni-MATH evaluations, substantially extending coverage of factual correctness, safety, difficult reasoning, and advanced mathematics.

E2.justification: Appendix M/Table 17 adds an evaluated DIV-REF comparator on SummEval and story generation using ROUGE, BERTScore, MOVERScore, and GPT-4-turbo. Original comparator sets remain unchanged. The Vanilla and Ref-based methods on the added reasoning benchmarks reuse established comparison strategies.

E3.justification: New protocols include GPT-4o correctness ratings on a 1-5 scale, aspect-specific multiple-reference evaluations, and ten-reference DIV-REF aggregation. Appendix O constructs positive-negative pairs through GPT-4o generation and oracle-guided correction, withholding oracle answers from judges. GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini configurations are also added; existing training and evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained bias, inference-cost, relevance, and revision-strategy analyses, Appendix J directly investigates error correction through LLMBar cases and correctness ratings. Appendices L-M test reference granularity and diversified-reference alternatives. These substantially expand analysis of whether and why the generated references help.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The existing three-cycle inference analysis is unchanged. New mean ratings and multiple-reference aggregation do not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Matched existing results retain their values, while v2 adds substantial results in Tables 3 and 14-19. Examples include reference correctness of 4.75 versus original-response ratings of 3.19/3.25, and GPT-4-turbo JudgeBench accuracy of 63.71 for ReviseEval versus 52.57 for the plain judge. New results are mixed: RewardBench reports identical GPT-4-turbo scores, and model labels in the final blocks of Tables 15 and 18 are ambiguous.

T1.justification: The original mathematical method and meta-evaluation definitions remain equivalent. Section 4.3 replaces the displayed pairwise indicator formula with its verbal description. Appendix P adds an informal segment-based mechanism illustration, without a formal theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims that response-adapted references improve LLM evaluation, activate classic metrics, and benefit weaker models. The revised conclusion adds prospective multimodal and multi-agent extensions without redefining the demonstrated core contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 and appendices J-P substantially expand interpretations of reference correctness and applicability to factual and difficult reasoning tasks. Appendix P newly argues that LLM training favors retaining correct segments and that retaining an error can leave evaluation unaffected. Some interpretations exceed the displayed evidence: Appendix N claims consistent RewardBench improvement despite identical GPT-4-turbo rows in Table 18.

D1.justification: New appendices specify the correctness rater and reviser, aspect-specific prompting, reference counts and aggregation, and GPT-4o response-pair construction. Existing prompt templates, training hyperparameters, decoding settings, and data-access links remain unchanged. These are targeted additions to reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations concerning multiple references, automated correction, and the new benchmarks. Appendix M explicitly distinguishes ReviseEval's response-conditioned references from DIV-REF's paraphrasing of pre-existing human references. The main related-work discussion and overall novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4.3 is reorganized around revision quality and reference effectiveness, evaluation descriptions are clarified, and the conclusion is shortened and given an outlook. Author/contact and publication-header text also change. Most existing prose and section organization remain intact; appendices J-P principally introduce new scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 adds a reference-quality summary table, appendix tables covering the new analyses and benchmarks, and two boxed correction examples. Figure 3 changes from a two-by-two arrangement to a much smaller single row with individual legends; Figure 2 marks retained text segments. Existing tables are also resized and reflowed, substantially changing the presentation.

improvement.justification: Direct reference-quality assessments, the multiple-reference experiment, and the DIV-REF comparison add targeted evidence missing from v1, while harder benchmarks better test applicability. The overall gain is limited by automatic correctness ratings without independent validation or uncertainty estimates, ambiguous model labels in Tables 15 and 18, and RewardBench improvement claims contradicted by identical GPT-4-turbo scores.
